channel.title: Cadence Evidence — PT Research Signal
channel.description: Daily curated physical therapy & rehab research for clinicians. AI-scored signal from 56 sources.

item.title: The effectiveness of proprioceptive training for the prevention of ankle sprains in athletes: a systematic review and meta-analysis
item.description: A systematic review and meta-analysis of 15 RCTs found proprioceptive training associated with a 34% lower relative occurrence of ankle injury in athletes, with moderate certainty of evidence.
item.author: BMC Musculoskelet Disord

item.title: Effect of Incorporating Perceptual Learning Into Plantar Hardness Discrimination on the Risk of Falling and Muscle Torque in Patients With Hemiplegia: A Randomized Controlled Trial.
item.description: A randomized controlled trial (n=34) found that incorporating perceptual learning into plantar hardness discrimination significantly reduced fall risk (P <0.001, ES=1.48), increased knee extensors torque (P <0.001, ES=1.19), and improved FIM scores (P <0.001, ES=1.56) in hemiplegic stroke patients compared to a control group.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Comparative effectiveness of different physical therapies for axillary web syndrome after breast cancer surgery: A network meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.
item.description: A network meta-analysis of 14 RCTs (1007 patients) found that soft tissue manual therapy + therapeutic exercise + low-level laser therapy significantly reduced pain (SMD = -4.40) and improved shoulder abduction (MD = 59.51) and flexion (MD = 77.30) in axillary web syndrome, while MLD + therapeutic exercise showed the largest improvement in upper-limb disability (MD = -19.01).
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Efficacy of Neuromuscular Electrical Stimulation (NMES) on Lower Limb Mobility and Activities of Daily Living in Post-Stroke Patients: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
item.description: A systematic review and meta-analysis of 10 RCTs (579 patients) found that NMES significantly improved Fugl-Meyer Assessment (MD=3.40, P=0.001), ankle dorsiflexion ROM (MD=1.56, P=0.04), TUG (MD=-1.96, P=0.03), BBS (MD=10.78, P=0.005), PASS (MD=5.05, P<0.00001), and MBI (MD=13.29, P=0.02) in post-stroke patients.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Effects of extracorporeal shockwave therapy on pain intensity and functional disability in chronic low back pain: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
item.description: A systematic review and meta-analysis of 9 RCTs (N unspecified) found that radial extracorporeal shockwave therapy (rESWT) significantly reduced pain (SMD = -0.72) in chronic low back pain, but functional disability improvement (MD = -6.12) did not reach clinical significance. Most outcomes were evaluated immediately post-intervention.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Physical activity guidelines' impact on cognition in multiple sclerosis: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized clinical trials.
item.description: A systematic review and meta-analysis of 12 RCTs (N=462) found that meeting physical activity guidelines for multiple sclerosis (PAG-MS) significantly improved processing speed (SMD = 0.29), visuospatial memory (SMD = 0.47), and verbal memory (SMD = 0.75) in individuals with MS.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Early supervised physiotherapy session-completion adherence and outcomes after acute lateral ankle sprain in professional athletes: concurrent indirect associations through kinesiophobia
item.description: A single-center retrospective cohort study (N=118 professional athletes) found that higher adherence to early supervised physiotherapy (per 10-percentage-point increase) was associated with a higher rate of achieving return to sport (HR = 1.27), lower odds of ankle instability (OR = 0.70), and lower residual pain (B = -0.36) after acute lateral ankle sprain. Kinesiophobia was identified as an important concurrent psychological correlate.
item.author: BMC Sports Sci Med Rehabil

item.title: Effects of treadmill exercise with and without vertical traction on gait, pain, disability, trunk proprioception, and depression in patients with chronic mechanical low back pain: A randomized controlled trial.
item.description: A randomized controlled trial found that treadmill exercise with vertical traction and partial body weight support (VT+TE) yielded greater improvements in gait, disability, and trunk repositioning compared to treadmill exercise alone (TE) or core stabilization in patients with chronic mechanical low back pain.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Long-Term Clinical Outcomes and Factors Associated With Response in Older Adults With Massive Irreparable Rotator Cuff Tears: A Four-Year Prospective Cohort Study.
item.description: A 4-year prospective cohort study found that the majority of older adults with massive irreparable rotator cuff tears responded well to nonoperative treatment, with significant improvements in shoulder function and pain persisting long-term. Longer symptom duration, smoking, and diabetes were associated with worse outcomes.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Comparison of short-foot and toe-curl exercises on movement control during single-leg landing after ACL reconstruction: An exploratory randomized controlled trial.
item.description: In an exploratory RCT (N=38 ACLR patients), short-foot exercise (SFE) lowered hip adduction excursion during single-leg landing at 6 weeks compared to toe-curl exercise (TCE), with a between-group difference of -6.30° (95% CI, -9.19 to -3.41; ES, -1.41), and this improvement was maintained at 12 weeks.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: A mobile-based multimodal monitoring system with clinician feedback for home rehabilitation after stroke: a randomized clinical trial
item.description: In a single-center RCT with 110 stroke survivors, a 6-week multimodal monitoring intervention significantly improved 6-minute walk distance by 23.15m (95% CI 6.70 to 39.60; p=0.006) and balance compared to standard care, with high participant satisfaction but mean adherence of 60%.
item.author: J NeuroEng Rehabil

item.title: A pragmatic, decentralized trial of the home-based, autonomous InTandem® neurorehabilitation system: analyses of engagement, safety, and effectiveness from the OrcHESTRAS trial
item.description: A decentralized trial of the InTandem® home-based neurorehabilitation system showed high engagement (81.9%) and significant improvements in 6MWT distance and TUG time in chronic stroke survivors.
item.author: J NeuroEng Rehabil

item.title: Measurement properties of observational gait analysis tools in neurological disorders: a COSMIN meta-analysis.
item.description: A COSMIN meta-analysis of 28 articles evaluating 7 observational gait analysis tools in neurological populations found no tool fully recommended. The Wisconsin Gait Scale (WGS) and Gait Assessment and Intervention Tool (G.A.I.T.) showed the best potential in stroke but had large measurement errors, suggesting use for group-level or cross-sectional analysis.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Effects of 12-week massage on pain, muscle co-contraction, and knee loading in medial knee osteoarthritis: a randomized clinical trial
item.description: A 12-week massage therapy RCT in 56 medial knee OA patients showed greater improvements in WOMAC pain, stiffness, physical function, and reduced medial muscle co-contraction compared to healthcare education.
item.author: Aging Clin Exp Res

item.title: Individual variability and predictors of responsiveness in physical outcomes following multicomponent physical training in older adults
item.description: In 314 older adults undergoing 12-month physical training, 46% showed high responsiveness across multiple outcomes, with multimorbidity, younger age, lower BMI, and higher resistance training adherence predicting better responses.
item.author: Eur J Appl Physiol

item.title: Construct validity and intrasession intra-rater reliability of the stair and step tests in individuals with multiple sclerosis.
item.description: This study involving 100 MS patients found the Stair and Step Tests have excellent test-retest reliability (ICC 0.997 and 0.955, respectively) and strong construct validity, making them practical for monitoring mobility.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Mediators of the effect of chiropractic care on 12- and 52-week outcomes for U.S. active-duty military personnel with low back pain: secondary analysis of a clinical trial
item.description: In a secondary analysis of a low back pain trial with US active-duty military, improvement in pain and disability during chiropractic care mediated 52-week outcomes for sleep disturbance and social role.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Validation and prognostic value of the five-repetition sit-to-stand test in patients with severe exacerbation of COPD.
item.description: A prospective observational study (n=58) found the 5STS test correlated with quadriceps force (r = -0.487) and 6MWT (r = -0.415) in severe ECOPD patients, showing acceptable prognostic value (AUC 0.720, 95% CI: 0.588-0.853) for predicting 6-month exacerbation-related readmission with a ≥13 seconds cutoff.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Predicting Robot-Based Tracking Performance After Stroke Using Lesion Features and Clinical Assessments: A Pilot Study
item.description: A pilot study (n=18) found clinical assessments significantly predicted robot-based tracking error (R^2=0.45) in chronic stroke patients, outperforming lesion features. Attention- and motor-related measures were identified as the strongest predictors.
item.author: medRxiv

item.title: Implementing low-cost Capability, Opportunity Motivation and Behaviour (COM-B) interventions to increase bed-substitution rehabilitation referrals in acute stroke care.
item.description: Low-cost COM-B interventions increased bed-substitution rehabilitation referrals in acute stroke care from 5.6% to 9.6% (p = 0.002) over 12 months in a study of 1146 patients (median age 65, 53% male).
item.author: PubMed
